content.title: About
content.content: The Bear is a soft plush toy made from hypoallergenic synthetic fleece. It is suitable for children aged 3 and up and serves as a perfect companion for sleep and play. The toy is filled with safe polypropylene fiber that retains shape and softness even after prolonged use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plush bears first appeared in Europe in the early 19th century.
Bears are believed to bring luck and comfort children during bedtime.
In Japan, “kinder bears” that emit gentle sounds when pressed are popular.
Bears are often used in therapy to reduce anxiety in children with autism.
The United States hosts an annual “Teddy Fest” where plush bear collectors gather.

items.title: Tactile development
items.content: The soft surface promotes sensory skill development in toddlers.

items.title: Emotional support
items.content: Having a favorite plush companion helps children cope with stress and fears.

items.title: Imagination boost
items.content: The bear encourages role‑play scenarios, fostering creative thinking.

items.title: Social skills
items.content: Play with plush characters aids the development of communication and empathy.

items.title: Safety
items.content: Hypoallergenic material minimizes the risk of allergic reactions.

items.title: Allergy to synthetic fleece
items.content: A small number of children may experience a reaction to the toy’s material.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small parts (e.g., eyes) can detach and pose a risk for children under 3 years old.

items.title: Wear and tear
items.content: With prolonged use the fleece may mat, requiring gentle washing or replacement.

items.title: Heat discomfort
items.content: Do not leave the bear in direct sunlight or near a heater to avoid overheating.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The bear can be cuddled, placed in a crib, used in role‑playing games, or serve as a decorative element in a nursery. If needed, it can be machine‑washed on a gentle cycle at no more than 30 °C.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bear in a dry place away from direct sunlight. For long‑term storage, place it in a fabric bag to prevent dust buildup.

content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas are a legume whose dried seeds are widely used in cooking. In this product a plant fat has been added, increasing its energy value and enhancing flavor. Chickpeas are rich in protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in ancient Egypt.
Dried chickpeas can be stored for up to a year when kept properly.
Added fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Chickpeas are a staple in vegetarian and vegan dishes as a protein source.
In some cultures chickpeas are a symbol of hospitality.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas contain about 20 % protein, providing a valuable source of essential amino acids for plant‑based diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports regular bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The carbs in chickpeas are digested slowly, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: The added plant fat supplies unsaturated fatty acids that are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Chickpeas provide iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking before cooking is recommended.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Added fat raises the calorie count, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause bloating and gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried chickpeas with added fat can be boiled, stewed, added to soups, stews, salads, or made into hummus. Soaking for 8–12 hours before cooking reduces cooking time and lowers phytic acid levels.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chickpeas in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.

content.title: About
content.content: Chitterlings are boiled or fried intestines (most commonly pork) that are a traditional dish in Southern US, Eastern European, and Asian cuisines. They have a strong aroma, a dense meaty texture, and are often served with spicy sauces or as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “chitterlings” derives from an old English term meaning “small things.”
In the United States they are traditionally prepared for Thanksgiving and New Year celebrations.
In some regions they are considered a delicacy, while in others they are known as “poor‑man's food.”
They can be cooked in many ways: boiled, fried, baked, or marinated.
In Japan a similar dish called “moto‑no‑ko” is often served with teriyaki sauce.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chitterlings provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good protein source.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Chitterlings are a source of iron, zinc, and selenium, nutrients important for immunity and blood formation.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: They fit well into low‑carb diets for those monitoring carbohydrate intake.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Intestines can harbor harmful bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli). Thorough cooking is essential.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to animal meat.

items.title: High cholesterol
items.content: Chitterlings contain a notable amount of cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should limit consumption.

items.title: Preparation challenges
items.content: Improper cleaning can leave bile residues, resulting in a bitter taste.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chitterlings are usually boiled until tender, then fried with onion, garlic, and spices. They can be served as a snack, added to stews, soups, or used as a filling for pies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh chitterlings in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2 days. Frozen portions last up to 3 months in an airtight bag. Before cooking, rinse thoroughly and trim excess fat.

content.title: About
content.content: French toast is a dish made from bread slices soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, sugar and spices, then fried on a pan until golden. It is traditionally served with syrup, berries, fruit or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in France in the 17th century and was originally called "pain perdu" – "lost bread".
French toast is often used as a way to rescue stale bread, turning it into a tasty and nutritious meal.
In the United States its popularity surged in the mid‑20th century with the introduction of ready‑made batter mixes.
There are many variations: with cinnamon, vanilla, rum, orange zest or even cheese.
In some countries, such as Japan, French toast is served with soy sauce and mayonnaise.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B6 vitamins from eggs and bread support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Improves iron absorption
items.content: Vitamin C from accompanying berries or fruit enhances iron uptake from the bread.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in the bread provide fast‑acting energy, making it a popular breakfast.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Frequent consumption with generous amounts of syrup or sugar can contribute to weight gain and blood glucose spikes.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: People with food allergies may react to these ingredients.

items.title: Trans‑fat formation during frying
items.content: Using oils heated to high temperatures can generate trans fats.

items.title: Gluten for sensitive individuals
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, so those with celiac disease should use a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat eggs with milk, add a pinch of salt, sugar and spices (cinnamon, vanilla). Dip bread slices in the mixture, let them soak, then fry in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until golden on both sides. Serve hot with maple syrup, berries, fruit or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared French toast is best enjoyed immediately. Leftovers can be cooled, placed in an airtight container and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or toaster to restore a crisp crust.

content.title: About
content.content: Fudgesicle Light is a frozen dessert made from low‑fat milk, with reduced sugar and a thin chocolate coating. It offers a smooth, creamy flavor with subtle cocoa and fruit notes, and a texture reminiscent of classic fudge.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fudgesicle Light was first launched in 2021 as part of the "light" line for calorie‑conscious consumers.
The recipe uses real cocoa butter instead of vegetable oil substitutes.
It contains 30 % less sugar than the regular Fudgesicle.
Each serving is coated with a thin chocolate glaze made without glucose syrup.
The product is certified gluten‑free and contains no artificial colorings.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced saturated fat helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Reduced calories
items.content: Approximately 120 kcal per serving, making it suitable for diet plans.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk contributes riboflavin (B2) and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa butter adds flavonoids that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains milk, so those with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein can trigger reactions even at small amounts.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although reduced, the product still contains added sugars, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Cold dessert
items.content: Consuming directly from the freezer may cause discomfort for people with sensitive teeth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fudgesicle Light is convenient to eat straight from the package. It can be diced and added to fruit salads, used as a cold topping for yogurt, or blended into a quick smoothie with berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen dessert in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After removal from the wrapper, it is best consumed within 30 minutes to preserve texture. Do not thaw and refreeze.

content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free salad dressing NFS (code 4991) is a light vinaigrette made from water, vinegar, aromatic herbs and spices. The product contains no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets and for people monitoring their energy intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat‑free dressing is frequently used in restaurants for “light” menu items.
The formula includes a vinegar concentrate that helps keep vegetables fresh.
It is very low in calories – about 10 kcal per 100 ml.
Without fat, the dressing does not form a film on the surface of salads.
Natural flavorings such as basil, oregano and garlic are often added.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The absence of fat makes the dressing suitable for reducing overall caloric intake.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Rich in aromatics
items.content: Herbs and spices provide antioxidant properties and pleasant taste without added sugar.

items.title: Diet‑friendly
items.content: No fat and low carbohydrate content make it compatible with keto and low‑carb diets.

items.title: Enhances vitamin absorption
items.content: Acidity of vinegar helps better absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from vegetables.

items.title: Herb allergy
items.content: The product may contain herbs that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions may have elevated salt levels; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drizzle over ready salads, use in marinades for fish or chicken, add to vegetable stews, or as a dressing for cold appetizers. Pairs well with leafy greens, tomatoes, cucumbers and carrots.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–8 °C. After opening, consume within 7 days. Do not freeze. Discard if color, odor or taste changes.
